# SK2190 — The struct key has no equality of its own

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A `Dictionary`, `HashSet` or `ConcurrentDictionary` is constructed over a source struct key that declares no equality member and is given no comparer, so every hash and every comparison goes through `ValueType`'s reflection fallback.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

`EqualityComparer<T>.Default` for a struct that implements nothing falls back to `ValueType.Equals` and `ValueType.GetHashCode`, which walk the fields with reflection when the layout is not blittable. The cost lands on every insert and every lookup for as long as the collection lives, and it lands boxed. ⚠ **The line where it happens contains no comparison to read.** A `Dictionary<Point, int>` names no method, so there is nothing at the use site for a reviewer to notice, and the declaration it comes from looks like an ordinary small struct — which is why the finding belongs where the collection is built rather than where the struct is written.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
struct Cell { public int Row; public int Column; }

var seen = new Dictionary<Cell, string>();
```

Write:

```csharp
readonly struct Cell : IEquatable<Cell> {
    public int Row { get; init; }

    public int Column { get; init; }

    public bool Equals(Cell other) => other.Row == Row && other.Column == Column;

    public override bool Equals(object? other) => other is Cell cell && Equals(cell);

    public override int GetHashCode() => HashCode.Combine(Row, Column);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **`SK2011` was read before this was built, and issue #4's premise about it is refuted.** The issue says `SK2011` reports at the declaration; `InheritedValueTypeEqualsAnalyzer` registers on `InvocationExpression` and reports at the `.Equals` call. So the comparison use site is already covered and this rule takes the use site where no comparison is written down at all. ⚠ **`CA1815` is not this rule, measured on a probe built outside this repository with empty `Directory.Build.props`/`.targets`.** At the SDK's default analysis mode it reports nothing — not at `Hidden` either, nothing in the SARIF error log; at `AnalysisMode=All` it reports on the struct's *declaration*, only when the struct is publicly visible, and whether or not anything ever hashes it. Different span, different trigger, off by default. Only `Dictionary<,>`, `HashSet<>` and `ConcurrentDictionary<,>` are recognised: `SortedDictionary` and `SortedSet` order their keys through `Comparer<T>.Default`, which throws without `IComparable` rather than falling back to reflection, and that is a different failure with a different repair. ⚠ **A constructor call that already passes an `IEqualityComparer<T>` is never a finding**, judged on the parameter rather than on the argument's type, because the comparer overload and the copy-constructor overload have the same shape at the call site. An omitted optional argument counts as no comparer. The key must be a struct **declared in this compilation** — a framework struct whose equality the author cannot change is not a finding anybody can act on — and must not be a record struct, a tuple, an anonymous type, an enum or a primitive, all of which have equality the compiler or the framework wrote. A type whose base list did not bind is withdrawn, the same discipline `SK2040`–`SK2044` use. ⚠ **A typed `Equals(Self)` with no `IEquatable<Self>` withdraws the type rather than confirming the finding.** `EqualityComparer<T>.Default` does ignore that method and does fall back to reflection, so the defect is real — and it is `SK2044`'s finding, reported on the declaration where the missing interface can be added. Report-only: generating equality members needs to know which fields define identity, which is the one thing a struct that declared none has not said, and adding a comparer is a decision about the collection rather than the type.
